summary: Seven new Polish, Japanese, Italian and Portuguese sources, including dissenting archival criticism and translation interviews. The inaccessible Ōe An Echo of Heaven review remains an uncounted lead.
next: Add non-European traditions and reader communities without relying on one translation outlet.

sources.title: Powieść jako forma sztuki
sources.note: Explores novels by visual artists, including Bruszewski’s multimedia fiction, Leto’s literary-film diptych and Niemczyk’s countercultural novel; expands form beyond conventional prose prestige.
sources.limits: Cultural promotion; book/film/artwork identities must remain distinct, English editions unresolved.

sources.title: Maria Kuncewiczowa, Cudzoziemka
sources.note: Czempinski analyses one-day recollection, musical and dreamlike structure, and Róża’s compelling yet destructive anger; contrasts Schulz’s psychological reading with later feminist emphasis.
sources.limits: Not Camus’s similarly titled work; historical reviews mediated through current critic.

sources.title: 日常生活の冒険 — 澁澤龍彦による書評
sources.note: Shibusawa praises Ōe’s lyrical urban rhythm and irony but finds its heroic-adventure claims and ending unconvincing; separates everyday observation from abstract philosophical rhetoric.
candidates: 日常生活の冒険 (Adventures in Everyday Life)
sources.limits: Reprinted review, not a newly independent 2017 judgment; English title descriptive, translation availability unverified.

sources.title: La Storia: Morante narratrice senza anagrafe
sources.note: Schilirò contrasts narrative voices across Morante’s four novels and questions the apparent omniscience of History; entertains Pasolini’s uneven assessment of its sections.
sources.limits: Quoted Pasolini criticism is mediated; realist appearance need not exclude fable.

sources.title: Elsa Morante e L’anno della Storia
sources.note: Scaffai examines Borghesi’s reconstruction of the History controversy: ideological allegiance and reactions to other reviewers sometimes displaced close attention to the novel itself.
sources.limits: Different review from Schilirò, shared publisher; historical judgments not counted as separate sources.

sources.title: A crítica de Guimarães Rosa
sources.note: Holanda traces Benedito Nunes’s interpretation of Rosa between poetic imagery and philosophical concepts; love joins the problems of evil, language and existence.
sources.location: Nunes’s critical method and love interpretation
sources.limits: Mediates earlier Nunes essays; neither their publication count nor quoted passages create extra sources.
